description:
Hi! I'm an enthusiastic and creative participant who enjoys exploring how technology, science and creativity can come together to create meaningful ideas. I'm particularly interested in space exploration, STEM education, digital storytelling and using AI tools to turn ideas into interactive learning experiences.

I'm developing SPACE GHOSTS: Abandoned, But Never Forgotten, an interactive educational website that brings the stories of NASA's forgotten equipment on the Moon and Mars to life.
summary:
# SPACE GHOSTS: Abandoned, But Never Forgotten

SPACE GHOSTS is an interactive educational website that brings the stories of abandoned space equipment on the Moon and Mars to life. Designed for children and curious space enthusiasts, it transforms NASA mission history into an engaging digital space museum.

Through interactive explorer profiles, mission timelines, fascinating discoveries and quizzes, visitors can explore the stories of four historic missions: Surveyor 3, the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Spirit and Opportunity. The website explains what each machine was designed to do, why it was sent into space, what it discovered and why it was left behind.

SPACE GHOSTS addresses the challenge by turning forgotten space hardware into meaningful storytelling experiences, helping users understand that even after a mission ends, its scientific contributions continue. By making NASA's space exploration history accessible, interactive and enjoyable, the project inspires curiosity, supports STEM learning and encourages the next generation to dream beyond Earth.

Their missions ended. Their discoveries didn't.
details:
Project Details – SPACE GHOSTS: Abandoned, But Never Forgotten

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

SPACE GHOSTS is an interactive educational website designed as a cinematic digital space museum. It allows users to explore the stories of human-made equipment left on the Moon and Mars after their missions.

Users can discover four historical space missions: Surveyor 3, the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Spirit and Opportunity. Through interactive mission profiles, users can learn about each machine's purpose, journey, scientific discoveries and mission legacy. The website also features a mission timeline, educational content and interactive quizzes to make learning more engaging.

2. What benefits does it offer?

The project makes space exploration history easier and more enjoyable to understand, especially for young learners. It transforms scientific information into simple, visual and interactive stories. It also highlights how equipment that is no longer active can still represent valuable scientific achievements and contribute to our understanding of the Moon and Mars.

3. What is the intended impact?

SPACE GHOSTS aims to inspire curiosity about space exploration, encourage STEM learning and help the next generation appreciate the achievements behind NASA's missions. It also promotes the idea that the end of a mission does not mean the end of its scientific legacy.

4. What tools, coding languages and software were used?

The project was developed as a web-based prototype using:

  • HTML – to structure the website and its content.
  • CSS – to create the visual design, layout and responsive experience.
  • JavaScript – to power interactive features such as exploration filters, mission information panels and quizzes.
  • NASA public resources – to research mission histories, scientific discoveries and obtain relevant educational information and imagery.
  • AI-assisted development – to support planning, content organisation, coding and refinement of the website.

5. How is the project creative?

Instead of presenting abandoned space equipment as forgotten objects, SPACE GHOSTS gives each machine its own story. Inspired by a futuristic NASA-style space museum, the website uses cinematic visuals, interactive exploration, mission storytelling and quizzes to turn space history into an experience. The concept encourages users to see these machines not as abandoned rubbish, but as silent witnesses to humanity's journey beyond Earth.

6. What factors were considered during development?

As an individual project, the main considerations were:

  • Scientific accuracy: Presenting mission information responsibly and using credible NASA sources.
  • Target audience: Making the content understandable and interesting for children aged 9–12 as well as general visitors.
  • User experience: Keeping navigation simple, interactive and easy to explore.
  • Visual appeal: Creating an immersive space museum atmosphere with clear text and engaging visuals.
  • Educational value: Connecting each piece of equipment to its mission purpose and scientific contribution.
  • Accessibility: Designing a responsive website that can be viewed on different screen sizes.
  • Future development: Allowing more missions, space objects and educational
